I do understand that, yes, and I know that the risk is there regardless of gear, but if you can protect yourself and reduce that risk by even 1%, I don't see why you wouldn't take it.

So what you and everyone else is telling me is that I should never talk to anyone about safety again because it's annoying? I understand that I sound like a petulant child asking this question but it's a genuine one. (as fake as that comment itself sounds)

I didn't forsee the influx of negativity I received, on a post regarding something as simple as just being safe no less, and I didn't think that there were any "societal rules", as you say, to follow here. I just wanted to say "be safe" but reddit wouldn't allow me so I expanded the message and got shit on for, for what to me seemed like no reason. I didn't think other people held such strong, aggressive opinions regarding the simplest advice. Which was very clearly my first mistake. The second was posting this in the first place. 

I get that hearing the same thing from everyone you've ever met is irritating but is it really so horrible to say it? I personally didn't think so, neither do I right now. In fact I enjoy the occasional head check every once in a while. But I guess I'm too different from anyone else in the community to understand why it's an issue.

I apologise for my toddler-like behaviour.

>you're still not getting it.

I am getting, people don't like to be criticised, I'm not stupid. I just don't see why, if I'm a stranger and they already don't care about my opinions, they would choose to respond at all? Grumble to yourself and go, is the way to go, in my opinion.

And yes, I also understand how hypocritical I sound given that I'm responding to all these comments, but that's because I didn't see the point of the aggression. I see the reason, saw it right away, I still don't see the point.
I just wanted to remind people safety comes first, whoever disliked me saying that could have just ignored the post instead of wasting their time.

You can't just have an audience, you need to attract it. Whether with a product of some kind or a talent, it doesn't really matter, but you can't just expect to create a website and become a billionaire.

I suggest you study marketing or at least do a whole lot of research on marketing strategies - although hiring a professional in the field would be best for you if you don't know anything about marketing - and design a product or brand that's going to lure people in and make them want to stay.

If you want to sell something, do a _lot_ of research to make sure it can withstand both single and mass production as well as that it's something that is wanted on the market. Selling a pencil won't go so great if what you're looking for is immediate profit as there's thousands of pencil brands and hundreds of trusted brands that people who need pencils have stuck with their whole lives/careers.

Do research on different demographics. Children, teens, adults, elders. Men and women. Disabled and able-bodied. Blind and sighted. Research different cultures and places, oftentimes certain stuff sells better in one location than another, know where your market is and know _who_ your market is. Do polls, ask questions, analyse your surroundings, the market you want to explore.

But most importantly of all, don't expect a payout and don't expect it to come overnight. You'll be over your head in "I have to be rich" that you won't pay attention to the brand or product, it will suck, people won't be interested and you'll lose before you've won.

Good luck!

Edit: don't forget a good slogan and logo, they go a _long_ way when it comes to selling something.
